newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Club agrees debt relief for Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club agrees debt relief for Tanzania.

text.p: The Paris Club of creditor nations said on Wednesday it had agreed to give debt relief to Tanzania, giving the east African country the most generous terms of debt reduction currently available to the world's poorest nations.

The agreement, which follows an accord in November with the International Monetary Fund on economic reforms, allows reduction on debt repayments of up to 67 percent, under so-called "Naples terms" of debt relief.
It covers payments due for the three years after the IMF accord and is meant to ease the burden of economic reforms.
Creditor countries agreed they could meet by the end of 1999 to consider any reduction in the stock of debt.
They could also undertake debt for nature, debt for aid, debt for equity swaps or other local currency swaps on up to 20 percent of the debt concerned, the Paris Club said in a statement.
Naples terms allow for a 67 percent reduction on either the stock of debt or on payments due.

The Paris Club is considering providing more generous debt relief for the world's poorest nations under an agreement reached last year for joint action between the creditors grouping, the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
It has not yet offered these enhanced terms, which could involve debt reduction of up to 80 percent.
